title: Project overview
keywords: what mediroute project about overview explain purpose works medicine delivery robot
answer: MediRoute is an ESP32-based medicine delivery robot. The supplied firmware controls two motors, reads two ultrasonic sensors, and accepts authorised RFID cards to send an unlock command to a medicine-box servo after a delivery cycle. Its web dashboard shows progress, sensor readings, RFID, servo and emergency-stop status.

title: Delivery timing and destination
keywords: delivery duration time timer seconds destination navigation mapping gps reached complete
answer: This version runs a 10-second delivery cycle. Movement, steering, obstacle avoidance and waiting all count toward those 10 seconds. Completion is based on elapsed time, not GPS, a map or a destination sensor. The firmware's destination-reached message should therefore be understood as completion of the timed cycle.

title: RFID access
keywords: rfid card authentication authorised authorized denied scan security rc522 access uid
answer: The MFRC522 reader compares a scanned four-byte UID with two authorised UIDs in the firmware. Unlocking requires an authorised card, a completed delivery, no emergency stop and a ready servo. This RFID check belongs to the medicine box. Dashboard face login is a separate feature.

title: Obstacle sensing
keywords: obstacle ultrasonic sensor sensors distance threshold detect avoidance hc sr04 filter median safety
answer: Two ultrasonic sensors monitor the left and right paths. The firmware samples approximately every 200 milliseconds, uses a median of up to five readings for display, and the minimum of the latest three valid readings for safety. Less than 30 cm indicates an obstacle; 40 cm is the clearance threshold. Stale readings cause a safe stop.

title: Motor movement
keywords: motor motors driver tb6612 steering move speed pwm avoidance reverse
answer: A TB6612FNG drives the left and right motors. The configured forward speeds are 190 on the left and 160 on the right, with an avoidance speed of 125. A left-side obstacle causes right steering and vice versa. When both sides are blocked, the robot reverses briefly and tests turning clearance.

title: Medicine box and servo
keywords: servo sg90 medicine box lock unlock opening angle feedback relock five 5
answer: An SG90 servo on GPIO 4 receives the medicine-box lock and unlock commands. The box is commanded to relock after five seconds. There is no physical angle or lid feedback sensor, so the dashboard reports a command being sent rather than confirming the box actually opened or closed.

title: Emergency stop
keywords: emergency stop safety restart reset halted button
answer: Emergency Stop sets a persistent emergency flag, stops both motors and prevents further movement and RFID unlocking. In this firmware you must restart the ESP32 to clear it. A completed delivery also requires a restart before another cycle can start.

title: Wi-Fi and dashboard connection
keywords: wifi wi fi wireless network connect esp32 dashboard ip offline internet status polling
answer: The ESP32 creates a Wi-Fi access point named MediRoute_Robot and serves its original dashboard over HTTP. The dashboard polls /status every 500 milliseconds. This companion dashboard runs on your laptop at localhost:8765 and can relay requests to the ESP32. Its face matching and built-in project answers run locally; microphone transcription also runs locally.

title: Face login
keywords: face facial camera login enrol enroll authentication recognition verification video privacy biometric
answer: The companion dashboard uses the laptop camera for enrolment and login. OpenCV YuNet finds a single face and SFace computes a face template. The server compares a new template with the enrolled one before issuing a dashboard session. Templates stay on this computer and captured images are not saved. This is a project prototype without certified liveness detection, so a photo or replay may defeat it. A recovery password is available.

title: Voice assistant
keywords: voice assistant audio microphone speech answers doubts ai chatbot talk model ollama
answer: Ask MediRoute accepts typed questions or local microphone transcription and can read answers aloud. The default mode retrieves curated answers grounded in the supplied firmware. It is not a generative AI model. You can optionally enable an installed local Ollama model for more flexible answers using the same project context. The assistant cannot operate the robot.

title: Limitations and improvements
keywords: limitations disadvantage disadvantages improvements future scope accuracy production hospital secure
answer: Current limitations include time-based delivery rather than destination tracking, UID-based RFID checks, no physical confirmation of the lid position, and no authentication on the original ESP32 endpoints. The companion face login is a prototype without certified liveness protection. Future work could add destination markers, lid feedback, authenticated firmware endpoints and evaluated anti-spoofing.
source: Review of supplied firmware and companion authentication design

title: Components
keywords: components hardware parts list microcontroller used requirements
answer: The firmware uses an ESP32, a TB6612FNG motor driver, two motors, two ultrasonic sensors, an MFRC522 RFID reader and an SG90 servo. The new voice and face features use the laptop's microphone, speaker and camera, with a local Python server.
